error.entity_not_found: Entity not found. Make sure the Sun integration is configured.

user.title: Pick the pergola and its sensors
user.description:
Choose the cover entity that controls your pergola, plus any optional sensors. The integration auto-detects the Home Assistant Sun integration.

Sun integration status: **{sun_status}**

data_description.cover_entity: The Home Assistant cover entity that tilts your pergola blades.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Optional. Lets the pergola detect when it's cloudy and stop chasing the sun. Use either a PV power sensor or an outdoor light sensor — both work.
data_description.light_sensor_entity: Optional. Alternative to PV power for sunny/cloudy detection.
data_description.humidity_entity: Optional. Pauses the automation when humidity is too high (e.g. during a storm).
data_description.rain_entity: Optional. Any on/off entity that reports rain — a rain contact on a smart input, a weather binary sensor, or a helper you debounce yourself. While it reads on, the integration issues no movement commands at all: your pergola's own controller has already closed the blades on its rain signal and would refuse them anyway.
data_description.priority_lock_entity: Optional. For pergola controllers (e.g. Somfy io) that expose a priority lock. The sensor must report exactly `rain`, `temperature` or `security` — any other state is ignored. `rain` holds position; `temperature` and `security` close the pergola. If you just have a plain rain sensor, use the Rain sensor field above instead.
data_description.priority_lock_timer_entity: Optional. Goes with the safety lock — remaining duration of the active lock, in seconds. Must be a plain number: a `timer` entity or an `HH:MM:SS` duration won't parse and falls back to 60 s.

geometry.title: Which pergola do you have, and which way does it face?
geometry.description:
Pick your pergola model from the list if it's there — published specs are filled in automatically. Then point your phone's compass app outward from under the pergola and enter the bearing.

Leave everything else at its default — the algorithm is pre-tuned for typical waterproof louver pergolas. Tick **Show advanced settings** only if you want to fine-tune the geometry yourself.

data_description.pergola_model:
Pick your pergola model to auto-fill the manufacturer's published specs (blade rotation angle). Pick *Custom / Other* if your model isn't listed or you'd rather measure yourself.

⚠ Only the Brustor B200 XL has been tested end-to-end on real hardware. Every other preset is sourced from the manufacturer's published spec sheet, but the algorithm itself was tuned for waterproof louvers similar to the B200 XL — non-Brustor models may behave slightly off until fine-tuned. If you spot an error or want a value adjusted, please open an issue at https://github.com/qelanhari/ha-pergola/issues with your model and the correction.
data_description.face_azimuth: Use your phone's compass app: stand under the pergola looking outward and read the bearing. 0°=N, 90°=E, 180°=S, 270°=W.
data_description.advanced: Reveals the blade geometry, summer/winter calibration, and sun exposure window. Most users don't need to touch these.

geometry_advanced.title: Advanced geometry settings
geometry_advanced.description: Fine-tune the blade physics and sun exposure window. Defaults match a typical waterproof louver pergola — change a value only if you know what you're measuring.

data_description.face_azimuth: 0°=N, 90°=E, 180°=S, 270°=W. Use your phone's compass app to read the bearing while standing under the pergola looking outward.
data_description.max_opening_angle: Mechanical blade tilt (in degrees) that corresponds to 100% on the cover entity. Most products report this in their spec sheet — leave 135° if you don't have the data.
data_description.calibration_offset: Permanent correction added to the computed blade angle. Increase (less negative) if blades close too much; decrease (more negative) if they close too little. Watch the pergola on a clear morning and tweak from there.
data_description.blade_pitch_ratio: How tightly blades overlap when closed: blade pitch (centre-to-centre distance) divided by blade width. Most waterproof louver pergolas are ≈0.92. Leave default unless you've measured.
data_description.flip_profile_threshold: Sun profile angle (°) at which blades flip from one side to the other. Calibrate by watching `sensor.pergola_profile_angle` — the value at which the first beam of sun starts to slip between fully-closed blades is your threshold.
data_description.summer_blade_offset: Tweaks the summer algorithm after the flip (phase B) only — doesn't change winter or morning behavior. Use positive values to close earlier in the afternoon.
data_description.phase_a_intercept: Where the morning ramp starts (% closure when the sun first hits). The pergola interpolates linearly from this value up to 100% at the flip angle. Raise it to keep more shade early; lower it to open more.
data_description.sun_az_min: Below this sun azimuth, the building itself shadows the pergola (eastern wall in the morning) and the algorithm falls back to the cloudy/standby position. Default = facing direction − 90°.
data_description.sun_az_max: Above this sun azimuth, the building shadows the pergola (western wall in the afternoon) and the algorithm falls back to the cloudy/standby position. Default = facing direction + 90°.

operation.title: How often should it run?
operation.description: Defaults are sensible — most users only tweak the cloudy/standby position or the humidity threshold.

data_description.update_interval: How often the control loop checks the sun and adjusts the pergola.
data_description.step_size: Blade position is rounded to multiples of this — reduces mechanical wear.
data_description.deadband: Minimum change needed to trigger a movement (small adjustments are ignored).
data_description.cloudy_target: Position used when it's cloudy, in standby, or outside the sun-exposure window. Default 60% is a sweet spot: enough shade for diffuse light, enough opening for a view. In summer it also caps the sun-tracking target: blades ramp up to this position (never past perpendicular) in the afternoon and rest there.
data_description.min_useful_percent: Below this target, the pergola switches to the cloudy/standby position instead — avoids tiny early-morning movements.
data_description.humidity_max: Above this humidity, the automation is paused (useful when a wet pergola shouldn't move).
data_description.min_elevation: Below this sun elevation (e.g. dawn/dusk), the control loop and morning calibration stay idle.
data_description.rain_clear_delay: How long the rain hold stays on after the rain sensor goes dry — stops a shower that flickers dry for a minute from resuming tracking immediately. Set to 0 if your rain entity already debounces itself.

cloud_detection.title: Cloud detection
cloud_detection.description: Tell us your inverter's nameplate peak power and the integration handles the rest. Tick **Show advanced settings** only if you want to fine-tune sensor geometry and hysteresis.

data_description.pv_max_watts: Maximum power your PV system produces under ideal conditions (the inverter nameplate value). The integration scales it for sun position automatically.
data_description.advanced: Reveals panel orientation, sunny-state thresholds, smoothing, hysteresis, and lux sensor settings.

cloud_detection_advanced.title: Advanced cloud detection settings
cloud_detection_advanced.description: Fine-tune sensor geometry and decision thresholds. Defaults work for most installs — change a value only if you have an unusual setup.

data_description.pv_max_watts: Maximum power your PV system produces under ideal conditions.
data_description.pv_panel_azimuth: Compass direction the panels face (0°=N, 90°=E, 180°=S, 270°=W). Defaults to the pergola facing direction — only change it if the panels are on a different roof slope.
data_description.pv_sunny_ratio: Fraction of modelled clear-sky power above which the sky is considered sunny. Lower = more often sunny.
data_description.pv_smooth_alpha: How much weight new readings get vs. recent history. Higher = more reactive to cloud changes.
data_description.hysteresis_duration: Minimum time before switching between sunny and cloudy states — prevents flickering during scattered clouds.
data_description.lux_sunny_ratio: Lux above this × sin(sun elevation) counts as sunny. Tune from a clear midday reading.
data_description.pv_observable_cos: Advanced — leave default unless the panel is mounted oddly. PV only votes 'sunny' when the cos(angle of incidence) on the panel exceeds this; protects against false-cloudy when the panel is too off-axis.
data_description.lux_az_min: Advanced — sun azimuth at which the lux sensor starts seeing direct sun.
data_description.lux_az_max: Advanced — sun azimuth past which the lux sensor no longer sees direct sun.
